target: branch (PO_0025073) as the whole of a count of parts: 'Leaves 2–5 per ultimate branch' = leaf (PO_0025034) part of branch, amount (pattern 03, 'part of' as in 'seeds per fruit')
reason: Not a bearer. It is a 'per X' phrase that names the whole the counted leaves belong to. 'Ultimate' (the last order of branching) has no position value in pattern 18, so it is dropped and the whole stays branch.

A synonym of corolla lobe in a sympetalous corolla. This follows the earlier review, which mapped petal lobe to corolla lobe. In a flora where the corolla is choripetalous the segments are petals (PO_0009032), so check the flora's family.

target: leaflet (PO_0020049) with 'has position' interjected (pattern 18). This needs a new position value 'interjected' (between the primary lateral leaflets), added to config/bearer_positions.tsv
reason: Narrower than leaflet. These are the small leaflets set between the main leaflet pairs, as in Solanum. Their counts ('0-14') must not be merged into the leaflet count, so plain leaflet is not enough. A position value is better than a new class.
Exact: a hyphenated spelling of the PO label.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part of bracteole (PO_0009043), the region pattern
reason: A region of an existing class. It follows the earlier rule that maps 'apex' to plant organ apex of the part being described.

target: plant organ margin (PO_0025005) part of calyx (PO_0009060), the region pattern
reason: A region of the calyx: its rim (wavy, ciliate, cuspidate). 'Bilabiate' and 'truncate' describe the calyx or calyx limb (FLOPO_0986093) rather than the margin, so better grounding of those statements could move them there.

Ambiguous. In the examples it is a collar of the anther ('collar de la antera') and a ring of hairs. PO's leaf collar is the grass leaf blade/sheath junction. Only a word next to it (anther, leaf, hairs) can say which.

label: sympodial unit
parent: is_a PO_0009006 (shoot system); part_of PO_0009006 (shoot system)
definition: A shoot system (PO:0009006) that is one of the successive units of a sympodially branched shoot: an axis produced by a single meristem, together with the leaves it bears, ending in a terminal inflorescence or flower, its growth continued by an axillary shoot. Should be proposed to PO upstream: the term is standard in Solanaceae, Boraginaceae and orchids, and PO uses 'sympodial' only in comments.
reason: A real module with no PO class. It is the whole that '2-foliate'/'plurifoliate' counts refer to (leaf part of sympodial unit, pattern 03), and 'geminate' describes its leaves as a set (pattern 16). It appears in only one flora here but in 171 statements, and the term is common.
Exact: 'anther thecae' is a PO synonym. '6-8-thecate' is a count of thecae per anther (pattern 03, compound word), like '3-foliolate'.

Narrower: a scale-like appendage of the connective. The family is unknown and the examples ('connective scales lateral') could mean scales next to the connective rather than on it, so check one source before adding the rule.

Ambiguous. 'Ray' can be an umbel or anthela branch, a ray floret or a ray of wood. Counts of 39-69 do not suit umbel rays in most families. Only 'amount' is attached, and there is no context to choose.

target: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) part of anther (PO_0009066), the region pattern
reason: A region of an existing class, like bracteole apex.

Nearly exact. In Poaceae the anthecium is the floret: lemma, palea and the flower they enclose. 'Neutral' and 'bisexual' are floret qualities. 'Upper/lower anthecium' maps to the floret with position upper/lower (pattern 18).

Narrower. In Mimosoideae floras, paraphyllidia are small stipule-like structures at the base of the pinnae; PO counts pinna as a leaflet synonym, so stipel is the nearest class. It is not the moss paraphyllium (PO_0030069). Check against the flora's glossary.

target: perianth (PO_0009058) in the fruiting state (pattern 04, state of the bearer)
reason: The persistent, often enlarged perianth around the fruit (as in Polygonaceae, Amaranthaceae, Nyctaginaceae). It is the same perianth in a later state, not a new structure.
Exact in meaning: a gland that secretes nectar. Position words ('basilar') go to pattern 18 or to 'part of' the organ that bears it.
Narrower: the pulvinus of a petiolule. PO's definition of pulvinus already includes the petiolule. Where the parent is needed it can be stated as pulvinus part of petiolule (PO_0020050).

target: seed (PO_0009010) with the surface region (the surface/region pattern of docs/annotation-context-patterns.md)
reason: A region of the seed. Its qualities (reticulate, pitted, alveolate, smooth) are surface sculpture. The testa (PO_0020057) bears this surface, but floras describe the seed.

Latin for 'sheath'. In diagnoses it can be a leaf sheath (PO_0020104), a stipular sheath or an ochrea (FLOPO_0986040). A sheath only 1.5-2 mm long is unlikely to be a grass leaf sheath. The genitive that follows it (foliorum, stipularum) has to choose.

target: petal (PO_0009032) part of pistillate flower (PO_0025599) (pattern 12, part of a qualified whole)
reason: A part of a qualified whole, like 'calyx of male flowers'.
Exact: a hyphenated spelling of the PO label. '8-10-seriate' describes the involucre as a whole (pattern 16).

A specific structure of one flora (Mimosoideae): a small point on the leaf rachis, at its apex or between pinna pairs. 'Present' and 'amount' rule out mapping it to the rachis apex. It could become a class 'rachis spicule' (part_of leaf rachis PO_0020055) if more floras use it, but that is not shown yet.

target: plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) part of bracteole (PO_0009043), the region pattern
reason: A region of an existing class. 'Connate' and 'free' describe the bracteoles as a set (pattern 16), but the region rule still holds for 'auriculate' and 'obtuse'.

'Scale' was rejected in the earlier review as a generic part that needs the organ it belongs to, so its margin is just as unresolved. Once the scale grounds from context, the margin is plant organ margin (PO_0025005) part of that class.
Exact: 'ovulate cone' is a PO synonym, and strobilus is synonymous with cone.
Exact: a spelling variant and the Spanish forms of pistillode.

'Ocelo' (eye-spot) is used for different things in different groups: a glandular dot on leaves, a spot on a petal, or a structure on a bract. Only presence is recorded, and the organ cannot be found from the word.

target: capitulum inflorescence (PO_0030121) as the whole of a count of parts: 'Florets c. 70 per capitulum' = flower (PO_0009046) part of capitulum inflorescence, amount (pattern 03)
reason: Not a bearer. It is a 'per X' phrase that names the whole of the counted parts, like 'seeds per fruit'.

target: filament (PO_0009067) part of stamen (PO_0009029) with 'has position' lower (FLOPO:0991377) (patterns 12 and 18)
reason: In a zygomorphic flower the anterior (abaxial) stamens are the lower pair, so 'lower' is the nearest of the nine position values. If anterior/posterior should be kept apart from upper/lower, a position value 'anterior' would need to be added.
Exact: the FLOPO class is defined as a raised part of the corolla's lower lip, and it had no bearer rule for this phrase.
